The möbius function is mu(1)=1, mu(n)=0 if a prime square divides n, and mu(n)=(−1)r when n is a product of r distinct primes. The Riemann zeta function is zeta(s)=∑n≥1​n−s for ℜs>1.
Both sides of the proposed identity are multiplicative. At n=pa, the right side is 1 for a=0,1 and 1+μ(p)=0 for a≥2, exactly mu(pa)2. Absolute convergence permits rearrangement, so
∑n​nsμ(n)2​=∑d​d2sμ(d)​∑m​ms1​=ζ(2s)ζ(s)​.
(1)

Paper 2 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 84
2I OurBigBook.com
Runge theorem says that if K⊂C is compact and C∖K is connected, every function holomorphic near K is uniformly approximable on K by polynomials.
Choose a compact exhaustion Kj​ of the slit disc Δ∖L+, rounding the two sides of the slit so that 0∈/Kj​ and C∖Kj​ is connected. Runge applied to 1/z gives a polynomial pj​ with supKj​​∣pj​−1/z∣<1/j. Every compact subset of the slit disc lies in all sufficiently large Kj​, proving locally uniform convergence.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

f(t)=2πi1​∫c−i∞c+i∞​eptf​(p),dp,
(4)
where the vertical bromwich contour lies to the right of all singularities. For t>0 it is closed leftwards, and for t<0 rightwards, where the exponential decays.
Transforming the PDE and imposing boundedness as x→∞ gives
U(x,p)=p(p+1)1​+p(p+1)p−1​e−xp/D​,
(5)
with the square root cut conventionally along (−∞,0]. Therefore
u(x,t)=2πi1​∫c−i∞c+i∞​eptU(x,p),dp.
(6)
There are poles at p=0,−1 (with cancellation assessed in the complete expression) and a branch point at 0; close left for t>0 and wrap the cut while including the relevant residues.

A branch point is a point around which analytic continuation changes a value; a branch cut removes curves so continuation becomes single-valued, and a branch is one such single-valued analytic choice. Define
Arcsinz=∫0z​(1−t2)−1/2dt
(10)
on C∖((−∞,−1]∪[1,∞)), choosing the square root equal to 1 at zero. Monodromy around ±1 explains multivaluedness.
On the upper lip 0+ of the cut convention, the branch remains positive on (0,1), so ∫0+1​dt/1−t2​=π/2. Define Arccosz=π/2−Arcsinz on the same slit domain.
Also
arctanz=2i1​[log(1+iz)−log(1−iz)].
(11)
Changing logarithm branches changes the value by multiples of π (already visible at z=1). Principal logarithms give a single branch on the plane cut from ±i outward. Differentiating both sides and checking the value at zero proves
Arctanz=Arcsin1+z2​z​
(12)
where the compatible principal branches are defined.
